newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon tries 25 as Israeli agents.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon tries 25 as Israeli agents.

text.p: Twenty-five Lebanese went on trial by military court on Monday, facing possible death penalties on charges of collaborating with Israel.
Accusations against them included supplying Israel with intelligence on anti-Israeli guerrilla groups and planning attacks on Syrian forces in Lebanon.
Lebanon and Israel are still officialy in a state of war despite five years of peace talks which are currently stalled.

Only four of the accused were in court. The hearing was adjourned after a brief session until November 4 after prosecutors argued that the other 21 accused still at large had to be served summonses informing them of the charges.
Three of the absentees were charged with planning attacks that included a failed 1988 assassination attempt against Brigadier Ghazi Kenaan, head of Syrian military intelligence in Lebanon.
The absentees included Akel Hashem, western region commander of the South Lebanon Army (SLA), a 3,000-strong client militia which helps Israel control hold a border zone in south Lebanon.
Abbas Dabaja, one of the four suspects in custody, is a local official of the Syrian-backed Amal Movement, which launches guerrilla attacks against Israeli troops in south Lebanon.

The indictment said Abbas visited Israel and gave "detailed information on south Lebanon villages, Amal officials' homes, resistance centres, weapons depots and all those working for the resistance and the internal divisions of the Amal operations room".

"Abbas informed the Israelis through new (radio) equipment of several military operations the resistance was planning, thus allowing the Israelis to take precautions, confront the fighters and kill them all," the indictment added.
